approaches.name: geospatial land information systems and digital records for land administration
approaches.description: The project uses CORS networks, satellite imagery, KoBo Toolbox M&E, and digitized land registries to support surveying, hazard modeling, and post-disaster tenure evidence. Practices: CORS network densification for geospatial positioning; Digital M&E system on KoBo Toolbox and geospatial platform for real-time monitoring of project-affected people and assets; Land Information System (LIS) in Wouri and Mfoundi land offices; Satellite imagery and geospatial modeling of climate hazards; Digitized land registry archives with climate risk data; Digitized land records for post-disaster tenure evidence.

extra_evidence.text: Building on the use of KoBo Toolbox and an electronic platform for land acquisition and resettlement screening, census, and valuation of Page 14 The World Bank Sustainable Cities and Land Project (P180884) affected assets in the preparation of RAPs, the creation of a digital M&E system can support real-time monitoring of implementation progress and project-affected people and assets.
GEMS could help build the capacity of the PIU and government agencies to use low-cost, open-source geospatial platforms such as KoBo Toolbox for digital data collection and analysis.
The project will use the Geo-Enabling Initiative for Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS).
